learn.title: Start investing in US stocks
learn.intro: The terms you will see most often in Pordee Port, explained briefly with diagrams. All examples use a made-up company and do not refer to any real stock.
learn.pe.title: What is P/E?
learn.pe.body: P/E (Price to Earnings) is the share price divided by one year of earnings per share. It tells you how many dollars the market pays for each dollar the company earns.
learn.pe.example: A made-up company trades at $50 and earns $2.50 per share a year → P/E = 50 ÷ 2.50 = 20
learn.pe.keep: A high P/E means the market expects strong growth. A low P/E may mean low expectations or higher risk. Compare it with companies in the same industry.
learn.pe.caution: Companies with losses have no P/E. The site shows "—" instead.
learn.div.title: Dividend yield
learn.div.body: Dividend yield is the total yearly dividend per share divided by the share price, as a percentage. It tells you how much you get back each year in dividends if you buy at this price.
learn.div.example: A made-up company at $50 pays $1.50 a year in dividends → yield = 1.50 ÷ 50 = 3%
learn.div.keep: US dividends have 15% tax withheld before they reach you. Pordee Port shows amounts before and after tax.
learn.div.caution: An unusually high yield can come from a falling share price rather than a bigger dividend.
learn.sma.title: 50-day and 200-day moving averages
learn.sma.body: A moving average is the average closing price over the last N trading days. It shows the overall direction by smoothing out daily swings.
learn.sma.example: 50-day average = sum of the last 50 closing prices ÷ 50. The 200-day average uses 200 trading days.
learn.sma.keep: The 50-day line reacts faster and shows the medium-term trend. The 200-day line moves slowly and shows the long-term picture.
learn.sma.caution: Recently listed stocks may not have 50 or 200 days of data. The site says "Not enough data" instead of drawing the line.
learn.rsi.title: RSI and the 70 / 30 lines
learn.rsi.body: RSI (Relative Strength Index) compares up moves with down moves over 14 trading days. It ranges from 0 to 100.
learn.rsi.example: RSI of 70 or more shows an "Overbought" badge. RSI of 30 or less shows an "Oversold" badge.
learn.rsi.keep: The badge says the price has moved strongly in one direction. It does not say when the price will turn.
learn.rsi.caution: At least 15 closing prices are needed to calculate RSI.
learn.cross.title: Golden Cross and Death Cross
learn.cross.body: When the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day average it is called a Golden Cross. When it crosses below, it is a Death Cross.
learn.cross.example: A cross counts when the 50-day line was below (or above) yesterday and is on the other side today. Being exactly equal does not count.
learn.cross.keep: It only says the medium-term trend changed direction relative to the long-term one. It does not promise where the price goes next.
learn.cross.caution: These signals usually appear after the price has already moved, so they always lag the price.
learn.delay.title: 15-minute delayed prices and Thailand time
learn.delay.body: Prices in Pordee Port come from the Pordee Mock Feed, about 15 minutes behind the live market. Every price is labeled with its time in Thailand time.
learn.delay.example: The market opens at 21:30 (standard time) or 20:30 (daylight saving time) Thailand time and closes in the early morning.
learn.delay.keep: When the market is closed, the price you see is the last session's close, with its date and time.
learn.delay.caution: A "Data not updated" badge means the source has not responded and the price is the last one received.
learn.screener.title: How to use the stock screener
learn.screener.body: The screener filters stocks by conditions you set, as a starting point for your own study. Results are not ordered by attractiveness.
learn.screener.step1: Set a maximum P/E, e.g. 20, to keep only stocks that have a P/E of 20 or less.
learn.screener.step2: Set a minimum dividend yield, e.g. 3%, to keep only stocks yielding 3% or more.
learn.screener.step3: Choose a market cap range if you want larger or smaller companies.
learn.screener.step4: Sort by symbol, P/E, yield or market cap, then open any stock for details.
learn.screener.keep: Stocks without P/E or dividend data are left out when you set that condition.
learn.end.title: For learning only
learn.end.body: Every number in Pordee Port is there to help you understand. Before investing, read from several sources and weigh your own risk.
